description: Indulge in the true taste of Liguria with this authentic Focaccia Genovese. This traditional Italian flatbread, known for its airy texture and crispy crust, is generously infused with fragrant rosemary and rich extra virgin olive oil. Perfect as an appetizer, side, or simply enjoyed on its own.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. This is the heart of your focaccia, so be patient.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Incorporate 2 tablespoons of the extra virgin olive oil into the dough. It will be sticky, but do not add more flour just yet.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for about 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. If it is too sticky, add a tiny bit more flour, but resist the urge to add too much. Form it into a ball.

instructions.title: First Proof
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place the dough ball in the bowl, turning it once to coat with oil. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes, or until doubled in size. For a quick focaccia, a warm spot is key.

instructions.title: Prepare for Baking
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Drizzle 2 tablespoons of olive oil into a 9x13 inch baking pan and spread it evenly. Gently transfer the risen dough to the prepared pan, stretching it to fill the pan. Use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the dough.

instructions.title: Flavor and Bake
instructions.text: Drizzle the remaining olive oil generously over the dimpled dough. Sprinkle with fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown and cooked through. The aroma will fill your kitchen with Italian sunshine!

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven and let it cool in the pan for a few minutes before transferring it to a wire rack to cool completely. Serve warm or at room temperature. Buon appetito!

tips: For an extra crispy crust, preheat your baking pan in the oven before adding the dough. This creates a thermal shock for a perfect bottom crust.
Do not skimp on the extra virgin olive oil; it is crucial for the flavor and texture of true Focaccia Genovese. Use a good quality, fruity oil.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh on the day it is baked. If you have leftovers, lightly toast them in a pan or oven to revive their crispness and aroma.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast of Italy, where a simple yet sublime bread reigns supreme: Focaccia Genovese. More than just a flatbread, this iconic Italian staple is a symphony of textures and flavors, renowned for its golden, crisp bottom, airy, tender crumb, and the irresistible aroma of fresh rosemary and robust olive oil. It’s a testament to the beauty of Italian baking, where quality ingredients and time-honored techniques transform humble flour and water into a masterpiece.

If you've ever dreamt of recreating that authentic Italian bakery experience in your own kitchen, perfecting the art of Focaccia Genovese is a delightful place to start. This article will guide you through the history, ingredients, and step-by-step process of crafting your own rosemary and olive oil-infused Focaccia Genovese, ensuring a taste of Genoa right at your fingertips.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?

Focaccia Genovese, hailing from Genoa in the Liguria region of Italy, is often considered the original and most authentic form of focaccia. Unlike its thicker, bread-like relatives found in other parts of Italy, the Genovese version is characteristically thinner, flatter, and boasts a unique dimpled surface. These dimples, pressed into the dough before baking, are crucial. They create little wells that collect a generous pooling of olive oil and coarse sea salt, which then crisp up during baking, contributing to its signature texture and intensely savory flavor.

The magic of Focaccia Genovese lies in its simplicity. It’s made from a lean dough – flour, water, yeast, salt, and copious amounts of high-quality extra virgin olive oil. The result is a bread that is simultaneously chewy and light, with a distinct crust that crackles with every bite. Traditionally, it's enjoyed plain, often dipped in coffee for breakfast, or served alongside meals throughout the day. Its versatility and irresistible taste have made it a beloved bread worldwide, but nothing quite compares to the authentic Focaccia Genovese, especially when still warm from the oven.

## Ingredients for Focaccia Genovese

The beauty of Focaccia Genovese lies in its minimal ingredient list, making the quality of each component paramount.

*   **All-Purpose Flour:** While some recipes call for bread flour for extra chew, a good quality all-purpose flour works wonderfully, yielding a tender crumb. Opt for unbleached flour if possible.
*   **Warm Water:** Around 100-110°F (38-43°C) is ideal for activating yeast.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** Ensures a light and airy texture. Instant yeast can also be used, often mixed directly with the dry ingredients.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** Incorporated into the dough for flavor.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** This is non-negotiable. Use the best quality extra virgin olive oil you can find, as its flavor is central to Focaccia Genovese. It's used in the dough, for oiling the pan, drizzling over the top, and even for dipping.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Sprinkled generously over the top, its aromatic piney notes perfectly complement the olive oil and salt. Dried rosemary can be used in a pinch, but fresh is vastly superior.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (e.g., Flaky Maldon or similar):** Crucial for sprinkling over the dimpled surface before baking. It provides bursts of salty crunch and enhances the overall flavor.

## Step-by-Step Focaccia Genovese Recipe

Crafting your own Focaccia Genovese is a rewarding experience. Follow these steps for a perfect loaf:

**Yields:** One 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) focaccia
**Prep time:** 20 minutes
**Rise time:** 2-3 hours
**Bake time:** 20-25 minutes

**Ingredients:**
*   3 ½ cups (420g) all-purpose flour
*   1 ½ cups (360ml) warm water (100-110°F / 38-43°C)
*   2 ¼ teaspoons (7g) active dry yeast (one standard packet)
*   1 teaspoon fine sea salt (for the dough)
*   ¼ cup (60ml) extra virgin olive oil, plus more for the pan and topping
*   2 tablespoons fresh rosemary leaves, roughly chopped
*   1 teaspoon coarse sea salt (for topping)

**Instructions:**

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water and yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Form the Dough:** Add the flour, fine sea salt, and ¼ cup of olive oil to the yeast mixture. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy, sticky dough forms. This is a high-hydration dough, so it will be quite wet. Do not worry about kneading extensively; just ensure all ingredients are combined.
3.  **First Rise:** Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
4.  **Prepare the Pan:** Drizzle a generous amount of olive oil (about 2 tablespoons) into a 9x13 inch baking pan. Use your hands to spread the oil evenly across the bottom and up the sides.
5.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently scrape the risen dough into the prepared pan. With oiled hands, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan. It might resist at first; if so, let it rest for 10-15 minutes, then continue stretching until it reaches the corners.
6.  **Second Rise & Dimpling:** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp tea towel and let the dough rise again for 30-45 minutes. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C) during this time. Once risen, uncover the dough. Drizzle another 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil generously over the surface. Use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the dough, pressing almost all the way to the bottom of the pan. These dimples are key for catching the oil and creating a crispy texture.
7.  **Top and Bake:** Sprinkle the chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt evenly over the dimpled surface.
8.  Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the Focaccia Genovese is golden brown on top and the bottom is crispy.
9.  **Cool:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia from the pan to a wire rack to cool slightly. This prevents the bottom from becoming soggy.
10. **Serve:** Slice and serve warm.

## Tips for Perfect Focaccia Genovese

Achieving that authentic Italian bakery quality is within reach with a few key tips:

*   **Hydration is Key:** Don't be afraid of a sticky, wet dough. The high water content is what gives Focaccia Genovese its characteristic airy, open crumb. Resist the urge to add too much extra flour during mixing or handling.
*   **Quality Olive Oil:** We can't stress this enough. A good extra virgin olive oil provides the backbone of flavor. Don't skimp! It's not just a fat; it's a flavor enhancer.
*   **Patience with Rising:** Allow the dough ample time to rise. This develops flavor and creates a light texture. Cold fermentation (a longer, slower rise in the refrigerator overnight) can further enhance flavor complexity.
*   **Gentle Handling:** Focaccia dough doesn't require aggressive kneading. Gentle folding and stretching are usually sufficient. Once it's in the pan, be gentle when stretching and dimpling to avoid deflating the precious air bubbles.
*   **Deep Dimples:** Really press those fingertips into the dough to create distinct wells. These pockets are where the olive oil and salt gather, creating delicious crispy bits.
*   **Hot Oven:** A hot oven ensures a quick rise and a beautifully browned, crispy crust.

## Serving Suggestions for Focaccia

Focaccia Genovese is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in countless ways:

*   **Plain and Simple:** The most traditional way – simply tear off a piece and savor its inherent flavors, perhaps with a drizzle of extra olive oil for dipping.
*   **With Meals:** Serve alongside soups, stews, or pasta dishes to sop up delicious sauces.
*   **Appetizer:** A fantastic starter with a platter of cured meats, cheeses, olives, and marinated vegetables. It also pairs wonderfully with balsamic vinegar and olive oil for dipping.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice horizontally and fill with your favorite sandwich ingredients – prosciutto, mozzarella, roasted vegetables, or pesto.
*   **Breakfast or Snack:** In Genoa, it's often enjoyed with coffee or as a mid-morning snack. Its savory profile surprisingly complements a hot beverage.

## Variations and Substitutions

While classic Focaccia Genovese is perfect in its simplicity, you can certainly experiment with toppings and slight variations:

*   **Other Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, fresh thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs can be used.
*   **Vegetable Toppings:** Before baking, press thinly sliced cherry tomatoes, caramelized onions, black olives, or roasted garlic cloves into the dimples.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano can be added with the herbs and salt for an extra savory kick.
*   **Flour Blends:** Experiment with a portion of semolina flour (up to 25%) mixed with all-purpose flour for a slightly different texture and flavor profile, common in some Italian breads.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While not traditional, gluten-free focaccia recipes exist using a blend of gluten-free flours, though the texture will naturally differ.

Focaccia Genovese is more than just a recipe; it's an experience. The process of making it fills your kitchen with the most enticing aromas, and the first bite of the warm, olive oil-rich bread is pure bliss. With this guide, you're well on your way to mastering this beloved Italian classic and bringing a piece of Genoa into your home. Buon appetito!
